title: Hosted API request clarity scoper and eligibility checklist
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Create a repeatable 'clarity scoper' checklist and eligibility rubric to triage enterprise-hosted API feature requests (especially multi-action chat streaming, function/tool-calls, and structured outputs). The goal is to reduce back-and-forth with customers, map requests to existing lanes (self-serve / dedicated / private), and surface blocking requirements (data residency, KMS, throughput/SLOs) earlier in the intake flow.
acceptance_criteria: A single-page checklist that PMs and intake engineers can apply to every enterprise request
A 0-20 scoring rubric that yields an initial routing recommendation (Self-Serve / Dedicated / Private / Needs Security Review / Not Eligible)
Set of 10 canonical clarifying questions to ask customers in the first 1:1 or intake form
Integration plan for the rubric into the intake form (Confluence/Drive template) and the intake dashboard used by Solutions and Sales
Documented fallthroughs and automatic follow-up templates for customers with missing information
scoper_checklist: Intent summary: What is the primary user-facing outcome? (generation, reranking, embeddings, multi-turn actions)
Interaction pattern: Single-shot vs streaming vs long-lived chat session vs toolchain
Data sensitivity: PHI/PII/regulated data? If yes, require Private deployment or explicit contractual controls
Latency SLO: p50/p95 targets and tail-latency requirements
Throughput: expected RPS and concurrent sessions (peak/steady)
Durability and audit: retention window for inputs/outputs and audit log requirements
Model needs: must-run model family or open to Redwood-verified variants? Need for custom fine-tuning or private weights
Tool/function calling surface: arbitrary external calls? must support structured tool schemas?
Cost sensitivity: threshold for per-token cost or monthly committed spend
Compliance & region: required cloud region(s) or on-prem constraint
eligibility_rubric: 0-4: Low complexity — Clear mapping to hosted self-serve; recommend quickstart + quota increase
5-9: Medium complexity — Possible hosted with guardrails (rate limits, model pinning); surface to PM for gating
10-14: High complexity — Candidate for Dedicated; needs infra sizing and SRE consult
15-20: Enterprise/Regulated — Likely Private or Dedicated with contractual controls + security review
clarifying_questions_template: 1) Describe the happy path and a common failure mode — what does success look like?
2) Expected sessions per minute and average tokens per session (including history)?,
3) Is streaming required for perceived UX? Acceptable fallback to chunked responses?
4) Do outputs need strict JSON/structured validation or are natural-language outputs acceptable?
5) Will tools be called server-side using customer-managed credentials? Are tool schemas standardized?
6) Any regulatory constraints (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2) or required physical region?
7) What is the acceptable cold-start latency (first token) and tail latency (95th/99th)?
8) Are customers expecting SLAs and uptime commitments? What penalty/recourse do they expect?
9) What volume/cost thresholds would force you to shift to Dedicated or Private?
10) Do you require log retention, audit trails, or per-token billing visibility?
triage_flow: Step 1: Intake form filled by Solutions or Sales with attached customer pitch and architecture sketch
Step 2: PM applies scoper checklist and computes rubric score (document in intake ticket)
Step 3: If score <=4, auto-assign to Growth/Onboarding with a self-serve playbook
Step 4: If 5-9, PM schedules technical discovery with Eng-RE and drafts a hosted mitigations plan
Step 5: If 10-14, open dedicated sizing ticket with Infra and SRE; estimate cost and lead time
Step 6: If >=15 or flagged for compliance, route to Security & Compliance and Solutions for Private deployment discussion
routing_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Prefer hosted solutions where possible to minimize lead time and operational overhead; fallback to Dedicated only when throughput or data isolation cannot be met reliably
Streaming UX often increases infra complexity — propose degrade-to-chunked responses as an interim to reduce Dedicated needs
Structured outputs may allow cheaper model variants with post-processing; when schema is strict, require stronger validation and regression tests
KMS/HSM requirements typically push requests toward Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys — include this early in the rubric
